name: chrome-offsets
title: Chrome offsets
description: Measures your fixed header and bottom bar and publishes their heights as CSS variables for sticky things to use.
docs: Wrap the page in ChromeOffsets and wrap each fixed bar in a ChromeOffsets.Top, Bottom, Start or End. A part measures what it holds, which is the fixed bar inside it; or give the part the classes that fix it (and as, to make it a header, nav, footer or aside) and let it be the bar. The provider writes --chrome-top, --chrome-bottom, --chrome-start and --chrome-end on its own element as pixel lengths, kept current with a ResizeObserver on every bar, so calc(var(--chrome-top) + 1rem) works for a sticky sidebar, a scroll margin, an anchored heading or the padding of the page. Bars on one edge add up, and an edge whose bars have all gone is zero. defaults (top, bottom, start, end in pixels) are what the variables are on the server and without JavaScript: set them to the sizes at rest. useChromeOffsets() returns the same four sizes as numbers, inside the provider. FloatingStack reads the variables when you pass respectChrome.
